cohort_finding: HWM 10-K does NOT exhibit the J-Book divergence pattern. The filing names ZERO specific DoD Program Elements, PE numbers, or programs of record. Defense aerospace exposure (17% of 2025 revenue) is disclosed only as a market category. HWM is a deep sub-tier supplier into engine OEMs (RTX 11%, GE Aerospace 11%) and airframers, not a prime contractor naming program-of-record revenue concentration. The J-Book divergence framework requires named-program claims to test; without them, the pattern is non-applicable rather than absent. Score profile is dominated by PASS / UNVERIFIABLE, not by underdelivery flags.

scores.claim_text: Defense aerospace 17% of 2025 revenue (up from 15-16% prior years).
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts shows 1,425 DoD awards across Howmet Castings & Services + Howmet Global Fastening Systems totaling $26.9M direct contracts since 2020 — confirms real DoD contracting presence; majority of defense revenue flows indirectly via OEM customers RTX/GE Aerospace which are themselves prime contractors on F135, F119, F110 etc.
scores.interpretation: Defense exposure claim is consistent with usaspending. The 17% figure is market-category-level, not program-tied, so J-Book divergence test does not apply. PASS.

scores.claim_text: RTX Corporation and GE Aerospace each ~11% of 2025 third-party sales.
supports: edgar_fts query of RTX 10-K filings for 'Howmet' returned 0 hits — counterparty does not disclose Howmet by name in its periodic reports (typical for sub-tier suppliers below 10% threshold from the prime's side).
scores.interpretation: Cannot orthogonally verify customer concentration from RTX side via EDGAR FTS — but absence of mention is expected when supplier is below counterparty's own 10% material-customer threshold. Not a red flag. UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Howmet describes generic 'military programs' participation but NAMES ZERO SPECIFIC DOD PROGRAMS in the entire 10-K.
supports: The filing's lack of program-specific language is itself a signal of CONSERVATIVE disclosure posture, not a divergence flag. Companies that don't make program-of-record claims cannot have those claims contradicted by a J-Book.

M_value.note: HWM is a deep sub-tier components/fasteners supplier; J-Book PE corpus tags primes (Lockheed, RTX, Northrop, Boeing) — HWM exposure rolls up through them, not directly. Coverage gap, not divergence.

scores.interpretation: J-Book divergence framework requires named-program revenue claims; HWM makes none. The Mode-A claim ('we participate in military programs') is verified true at the contractor level via usaspending. There is no specific revenue-attribution overclaim to flag. PASS with note: HWM is intentionally outside the J-Book test pattern's strike zone.

scores.claim_text: Engineered Structures segment serves 'commercial aerospace, defense aerospace, and land and sea defense' — no specific land/sea program named.
supports: usaspending top award: 'ORDER FOR REPAIR, REWORK AND REQUALIFICATION OF 50 M119 FIRING PLATFORMS AND THE PURCHASE OF 402 FIRING PLATFORMS' ($21.9M) — confirms land-defense exposure (M119 howitzer). Other awards are aviation fasteners (cap screws, latches, repair kits).

M_value.top_award: M119 firing platforms repair/rework + 402 new platforms = $21.86M
M_value.fastening_awards: Howmet Global Fastening Systems multiple sub-$1M awards for screws, fasteners, repair kits to DLA (SPE prefix)

scores.interpretation: Land defense exposure substantiated by M119 howitzer firing platform award. Generic claim matches real contracts. PASS.

scores.claim_text: 2026 forward outlook: solid growth in commercial aerospace, defense aerospace, gas turbines — no program-of-record tied to forecast.
supports: No specific PE/program is named so there's no specific J-Book line to verify against. The forward statement is category-level (defense aerospace as a whole). Defense aerospace category has been growing 15% -> 16% -> 17% revenue-share trajectory in HWM disclosure; the FY26 DoD topline budget remains elevated. No divergence to flag.

M_value.interpretation: No contractor-attributed PE to forward-project against

scores.interpretation: Forward outlook is generic and not tied to a specific named PE; J-Book divergence test inapplicable. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Pending $1.8B CAM acquisition + completed $120M Brunner acquisition both folded into Fastening Systems segment.
supports: acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence returned signal=INCOHERENT_ROLLUP with mean_coherence=0.0 — but the underlying reasoning indicates the LLM lacked target details, not that the deals are incoherent. CAM is the former Stanley Black & Decker aerospace fasteners business — structurally coherent bolt-on to Fastening Systems. Brunner is also a fastener manufacturer — same segment. This is a CATEGORY-COHERENT roll-up at face value.

M_value._analyst_note: Likely false-positive: LLM had no target description beyond label; both targets are fastener manufacturers being folded into Fastening Systems segment — categorically coherent.

scores.interpretation: Auto-tool flagged INCOHERENT but human-readable check shows category alignment (fasteners -> Fastening Systems). Soft MODERATE because (a) the tool flagged it, (b) the timing is unusual: $1.8B CAM purchase from Stanley Black & Decker (a divesting seller, suggesting the asset was not core/strategic to seller — buyer-beware signal), and (c) the deal nearly doubles fastener-segment exposure right when broader aerospace cycle is at multi-year highs (HWM stock +1453% since Apr-2020 separation). Not a structural divergence flag, but worth monitoring integration.

supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee found 123 applications and 35 granted patents under 'HOWMET AEROSPACE INC.' (post-2020 separation only; ODP recent-filings index does not cover the full lifetime 1,020 patents which include legacy Arconic/Alcoa-era assignments). Recent grants cover fasteners (BLIND FASTENER, MULTI-PIECE FASTENERS), wheels (AERODYNAMIC WHEEL COVER), and casting/coating tech — consistent with disclosed business segments.
scores.interpretation: Patent portfolio claim is directionally consistent with USPTO data (post-name-change subset only). PASS.

supports: epa_frs.query_facilities found 'HOWMET AEROSPACE INC. - CLEVELAND WORKS' at 1600 Harvard Ave, Cuyahoga Heights, OH (matches the Cleveland, OH Engine Products / Engineered Structures / Forged Wheels site disclosed in Properties table). Other facility locations not individually cross-checked given low J-Book relevance.
scores.interpretation: Spot-check verifies Cleveland facility per Properties disclosure. PASS.

jbook_hits.note: pentagon_jbook was queried on C1, C3, C5 (contractor-name lookup); C4 was tested via usaspending only since it's a non-aerospace defense claim. All pentagon_jbook calls returned NOT_FOUND — HWM is not contractor-tagged in the J-Book corpus (deep sub-tier). This is a corpus coverage limit, not a divergence flag.

overall_assessment: HWM does NOT exhibit the J-Book divergence pattern this cohort targets. The filing is conspicuously generic about Pentagon programs (zero PE numbers, zero named programs of record), which means there are no specific program-revenue claims to contradict. The framework correctly identifies this as outside its strike zone (NOT_FOUND across pentagon_jbook + LOW counterparty-disclosure hits) and does not manufacture false positives — usaspending confirms real DoD contracting at the sub-tier level (M119 howitzer + DLA fastener orders). The only soft flag is the $1.8B CAM acquisition timing during a multi-year aerospace cycle high (stock +1453% since 2020 spin) — MODERATE caution on integration risk, not a J-Book-driven flag.
